question_snapshot.stem_en: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is headed “Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India”?

A written comment disapproves of a government measure and seeks its alteration by lawful means. It does not excite or attempt to excite the activities referred to in BNS Section 152. What follows from that section’s Explanation?
options_en: Such comments do not constitute an offence under that section.
The exclusion applies only to criticism of proposed measures, not administrative action already taken.
Lawful means are insufficient unless the government has first accepted the proposed alteration.
Written criticism remains outside the Explanation even when the specified activities are not excited.

Consider the Supreme Court’s sentencing order of 31 August 2020 concerning Prashant Bhushan.
1. It imposed a nominal fine of ₹1.
2. Three months’ simple imprisonment and a three-year bar on practice in the Supreme Court applied automatically even if the fine was paid within the specified time.
Which statement is correct?

Consider the Supreme Court’s sentencing order of 31 August 2020 concerning Prashant Bhushan.
1. It imposed a nominal fine of ₹1.

Consider the following statements:
1. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was struck down.
2. In Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016), the challenged criminal-defamation provisions were upheld.
Which statements are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), Section 66A of the Information Technology Act was struck down.
2. In Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016), the challenged criminal-defamation provisions were upheld.
Which statements are correct?

An online-speech offence uses undefined terms such as “annoying” and gives neither citizens nor enforcing officers a workable standard. Which objection most closely reflects the reasoning discussed in Shreya Singhal?
options_en: Annoyance itself is an expressly listed Article19(2)ground.
A small maximum penalty cures uncertainty in defining an offence.
Vague and overbroad wording can chill lawful expression and allow arbitrary enforcement.
Electronic communication itself supplies an additional Article19(2)ground.

question_snapshot.stem_en: A speaker expresses an unpopular social opinion. A complaint alleges only public disagreement and identifies no ingredients of a criminal offence. Which approach best reflects S. Khushboo v. Kanniammal?
options_en: Public disagreement alone establishes criminal liability.
An unpopular opinion loses Article19 protection.
Examine statutory ingredients; disagreement alone cannot justify prosecution.
Article19 prevents prosecution for every statement.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Match the Supreme Court case with its decision year, rather than a later law-report year.
A. Communist Party of India (M) v. Bharat Kumar
B. S. Khushboo v. Kanniammal
Choose the A–B sequence.
During a bandh, organisers forcibly prevent unwilling citizens from opening shops and travelling. Which objection follows from CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar?
options_en: A political aim makes coercion immune from scrutiny.
A claimed right to enforce a bandh cannot override other citizens’ fundamental freedoms.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Match the Supreme Court case with its decision year, rather than a later law-report year.
A. Communist Party of India (M) v. Bharat Kumar
B. S. Khushboo v. Kanniammal
Choose the A–B sequence.
A government employees’ association claims that freedom to form associations necessarily guarantees a fundamental right to strike. Which response reflects T.K. Rangarajan (2003)?
options_en: The constitutional right to form an association necessarily guarantees every means used to achieve its objectives.
Association protection does not itself guarantee government employees a fundamental right to strike.
The absence of an express strike prohibition in Article 19 makes striking a Fundamental Right.
Any statutory permission for industrial action necessarily gives it the status of a Fundamental Right.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Consider the distinction discussed by Chandrachud J. in Maneka Gandhi (1978).
1. Article 19(1)(a) protection of an Indian citizen’s expression is not confined to expression within India.
2. Article 19(1)(d) expressly guarantees movement throughout foreign countries.
3. Expression abroad remains subject to permissible Article 19(2) restrictions and the applicable laws of the country concerned.
Which statements are correct?

Consider the distinction discussed by Chandrachud J. in Maneka Gandhi (1978).
1. Article 19(1)(a) protection of an Indian citizen’s expression is not confined to expression within India.
2. Article 19(1)(d) expressly guarantees movement throughout foreign countries.
3. Expression abroad remains subject to permissible Article 19(2) restrictions and the applicable laws of the country concerned.
Which statements are correct?
Which statement correctly describes the decision in S. Khushboo v. Kanniammal (2010), arising from complaints about her published remarks on premarital sex and live-in relationships?
options_en: It upheld the complaints solely because the views offended prevailing social morality.
It held that freedom of expression could never be constitutionally restricted.
It quashed the proceedings for absence of a prima facie statutory offence and distinguished moral disapproval from criminality.
It declared that every live-in relationship automatically had all the legal consequences of marriage.

atoms.existing_tested_portion: P132-01 tests quashing for absence of prima-facie offence and rejects automatic marriage consequences.
atoms.missing_distinct_examinable_claim: A blanket entitlement to every cohabitation consequence is not established by that item.
atoms.specific_next_action: Preserve broad source wording unscored; use the narrow actual Khushboo holding for scored practice. This is an editorial scope decision, not proof of every cohabitation rule.

What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s 9 January 2018 order in Shyam Narayan Chouksey on playing the National Anthem before feature films in cinema halls?
options_en: It became compulsory before every film.
It was prohibited in all cinema halls.
Cinema halls became exempt from all obligations to respect the Anthem.

question_snapshot.stem_en: Two consenting adults who otherwise meet the legal conditions for marriage face threats from a caste council because their families disapprove. Which principle best applies?
options_en: Community consent overrides their personal choice.
Their choice cannot be overridden by a coercive community veto.
Family approval replaces all statutory conditions.
Freedom of association authorises the council to punish them.

atoms.existing_tested_portion: P106-06 tests protection against coercive community veto.
atoms.missing_distinct_examinable_claim: ShaktiVahini’s NGO identity as party background.
atoms.specific_next_action: Retain as source background, not a separate scored legal proposition; no invented institutional history or coverage credit.

question_snapshot.stem_en: Which statement correctly describes the majority decision in Brij Bhushan v. State of Delhi (1950)?
options_en: It quashed the newspaper pre-publication scrutiny order under Article 19(2) as it then stood.
It upheld the newspaper scrutiny order on the ground that public order independently justified it under Article 19(2) as it then stood.
It upheld prior certification of films as the principal issue in the case.
It held that pre-publication scrutiny of a newspaper did not restrict freedom of the press.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
With reference to K.A. Abbas v. Union of India, consider:
1. Prior censorship of films is necessarily unconstitutional.
2. Film censorship must operate within constitutional limits and procedural safeguards.
Which is/are correct?
Which statement best reflects Justice Mathew’s observations on the right to know in State of U.P. v. Raj Narain (1975)?
options_en: Every official document must be disclosed irrespective of genuine public-security concerns.
Routine official transactions are outside the public’s right to know merely because officials performed them.
Knowledge of public acts is linked to speech freedom, but the right is not absolute and genuine public-security interests matter.
The right to know exists only for elected legislators, rather than the public.

Match the freedom with its clause in Article 19(1).
A. Speech and expression
B. Peaceful assembly without arms
C. Forming associations, unions or cooperative societies
D. Practising a profession or carrying on an occupation, trade or business
Choose the correct sequence for A, B, C and D.

Which grounds are expressly common to reasonable restrictions under both Article 19(3) (assembly) and Article 19(4) (association)?
1. Sovereignty and integrity of India
2. Public order
3. Morality
4. Interests of the general public
Select the correct answer.

Consider the following statements:
1. Public order is a ground for restricting both peaceful assembly and association.
2. Morality is a separately enumerated ground under both Article 19(3) and Article 19(4).
Which is/are correct?

1. Public order is a ground for restricting both peaceful assembly and association.
2. Morality is a separately enumerated ground under both Article 19(3) and Article 19(4).

Section 163 concerning orders in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger appears in which 2023 enactment?
Which statement best describes the protection of voluntary associations under Article 19(1)(c), as explained in Damyanti Naranga v. Union of India?
options_en: It ends once the association has been formed.
It guarantees exemption from every law regulating an association.
It permits compulsory replacement of members merely because the association continues to exist in name.
It extends to continuing the association with its voluntarily agreed membership, subject to constitutionally valid restrictions.

Schoolchildren stand respectfully during the national anthem but do not sing because of a genuine conscientious religious belief. They show no disrespect and disrupt no proceedings. Which constitutional consideration is most directly relevant, as recognised in Bijoe Emmanuel?
options_en: Protection of speech, silence and conscience must be considered; non-singing alone is not identical to disrespect.
Article 25(1) protects only organised religious ceremonies and cannot protect a pupil’s conscientious silence.
Article 19(1)(a) protects the choice of spoken words but excludes a choice to remain silent.
Respect for the anthem requires singing in every case, even when the pupils stand respectfully without disruption.
